audits.title: Time to ward transfer for acute hip fracture from the emergency department
audits.standard: BOA and BGS Blue Book, ward within four hours

cycle1.result: Mean time to orthopaedic review 83 min; mean time to ward 417 min

audits.intervention: On-call orthopaedics review suspected hip fractures before full workup

cycle2.result: Review 76 min, ward 333 min; when trainees on call, review 37.5 min and ward 294 min

audits.other_findings: Still well above four hours after the change
audits.fix_type_note: classified by Claude from the intervention described

audits.title: 52 AUDIT CYCLE EXAMINING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT POST EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT MULTI-DISCIPLINARY SIMULATION BASED MEDICAL EDUCATION TRAINING ON HIP FRACTURE CARE
audits.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of attending ED
audits.setting: Emergency department, Tallaght University Hospital, Dublin

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% (8/31) reached ward <4 hours

audits.intervention: 90 minute multidisciplinary simulation training programme on the hip fracture pathway for ED and related staff (32 people), in person and via Zoom, February 2021

cycle2.result: Average time to ward 5 hrs 58 mins (32% reduction); 72% (18/25) reached ward <4 hours

audits.other_findings: Training included Emergency Medicine, Orthopaedics, nursing, Radiology, Radiography and porters.
audits.citation: Clancy C, Mahony R, Meighan V. 52 AUDIT CYCLE EXAMINING QUALITY IMPROVEMENT POST EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT MULTI-DISCIPLINARY SIMULATION BASED MEDICAL EDUCATION TRAINING ON HIP FRACTURE CARE. Age and Ageing. 2021;50(Supplement_3):ii9-ii41. doi:10.1093/ageing/afab219.52.

audits.title: 695 QUALITY IMPROVEMENT PROJECT ON TRANSFER TIMES OF ACUTE HIP FRACTURE PATIENTS FROM ED TO INPATIENT BED POST SIMULATION TRAINING
audits.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: admission to an orthopaedic ward bed within 4 hours of ED attendance
audits.setting: Emergency department, TUH (Tallaght University Hospital), proximal femoral fractures

cycle1.result: Average time to ward 8 hrs 29 mins; 26% of patients reached ward (within standard).

audits.intervention: 90-minute multidisciplinary simulation training on the hip fracture pathway for ED staff (32 people; in person and via Zoom), February 2021.

cycle2.result: Not reported in abstract (text truncated); authors conclude improved time to ward and compliance with IHFS 1.

audits.title: Delving Deeper into Audit to Co-Design a Digital Solution to Improve “Time to Bed” – Irish Hip Fracture Standard
audits.standard: Irish Hip Fracture Standard 1: dedicated orthopaedic bed within 4 hours of ED arrival
audits.setting: Model 4 Trauma Centre, Cork University Hospital

cycle1.result: Fewer than 41% reached an orthopaedic bed within 4 hours (national average 36%); mean 3 hours from arrival to specialist assessment.

audits.other_findings: Delays mainly before X-ray and orthopaedic review, with duplicated digital and paper documentation; a co-designed digital admission proforma is being developed.
audits.citation: Stanley E, O’Keeffe T, Fogarty E, Misca L, Urtila V, Iliescu A, et al.. Delving Deeper into Audit to Co-Design a Digital Solution to Improve “Time to Bed” – Irish Hip Fracture Standard. Age and Ageing. 2026;55(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/ageing/afag197.040.

audits.title: Audit of the effect of a fast tracking protocol on transfer time from A&E to ward for patients with hip fractures.
audits.standard: Transfer from A&E to ward within 1 hour
audits.setting: Alexandra Hospital, Redditch, district general hospital, A&E department

cycle1.result: Mean transfer time 2 h 45 min ± 57 min (median 2 h 40 min); 3/104 within 1 hour.

audits.intervention: Fast tracking protocol for transfer of hip fracture patients from A&E to ward, implemented December 1997.

cycle2.result: Mean 1 h 32 min ± 40.87 min (median 1 h 25 min), p<0.001; 24/90 within 1 hour, p<0.001.

audits.other_findings: 10 of 100 patients not fast tracked (multiple injuries, medical problems, unclear diagnosis) averaged 2 h 55 min in A&E.
audits.citation: Rajmohan B. Audit of the effect of a fast tracking protocol on transfer time from A&E to ward for patients with hip fractures. Injury. 2000;31(8):585-589. doi:10.1016/s0020-1383(00)00056-5. PMID: 10986371.
